name: davidkimai/Context-Engineering description: "Context engineering is the delicate art and science of filling the context window with just the right information for the next step." — Andrej Karpathy. A frontier, first-principles handbook inspired by Karpathy and 3Blue1Brown for moving beyond prompt engineering to the wider discipline of context design, orchestration, and optimization. --
# Context Engineering
> **"Context engineering is the delicate art and science of filling the context window with just the right information for the next step." — [**Andrej Karpathy**](https://x.com/karpathy/status/1937902205765607626)** > > [**Software Is Changing (Again) Talk @YC AI Startup School**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LCEmiRjPEtQ)
## [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/davidkimai/Context-Engineering)
## [DeepGraph](https://www.deepgraph.co/davidkimai/Context-Engineering) ## [Chat with NotebookLM + Podcast Deep Dive](https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/0c6e4dc6-9c30-4f53-8e1a-05cc9ff3bc7e) ## [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20chat-7289DA.svg?logo=discord")](https://discord.gg/JeFENHNNNQ)
## [Comprehensive Course Under Construction](https://github.com/davidkimai/Context-Engineering/tree/main/00_COURSE) > ### **[Context Engineering Survey-Review of 1400 Research Papers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.13334)** > > [**Awesome Context Engineering Repo**](https://github.com/Meirtz/Awesome-Context-Engineering) Operationalizing the Latest Research on Context With First Principles & Visuals — July 2025 from ICML, IBM, NeurIPS, OHBM, and more > **"Providing “cognitive tools” to GPT-4.1 increases its pass@1 performance on AIME2024 from 26.7% to 43.3%, bringing it very close to the performance of o1-preview."** — [**IBM Zurich**](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.12115)
## [`Agent Commands`](https://github.com/davidkimai/Context-Engineering/tree/main/.claude/commands) **Support for [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) | [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) | [Amp](https://sourcegraph.com/amp) | [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/) | [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) | [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)** #### [Context Engineering Survey-Review of 1400 Research Papers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.13334) | [Context Rot](https://research.trychroma.com/context-rot) | [IBM Zurich](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.12115) | [Quantum Semantics](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.10077) | [Emergent Symbolics ICML Princeton](https://openreview.net/forum?id=y1SnRPDWx4) | [MEM1 Singapore-MIT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.15841) | [LLM Attractors Shanghai AI](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.15208?) | [MemOS Shanghai](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS) | [Latent Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.06203) | [Dynamic Recursive Depths](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.10524)
A frontier, first-principles handbook for moving beyond prompt engineering to the wider discipline of context design, orchestration, and optimization. ``` Prompt Engineering │ Context Engineering ↓ │ ↓ "What you say" │ "Everything else the model sees" (Single instruction) │ (Examples, memory, retrieval, │ tools, state, control flow) ``` ## Definition of Context Engineering > **Context is not just the single prompt users send to an LLM. Context is the complete information payload provided to a LLM at inference time, encompassing all structured informational components that the model needs to plausibly accomplish a given task.** > > — [**Definition of Context Engineering from A Systematic Analysis of Over 1400 Research Papers**](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.13334) ``` ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ CONTEXT ENGINEERING MASTERY COURSE │ │ From Zero to Frontier │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ▲ │ Mathematical Foundations C = A(c₁, c₂, ..., cₙ) │ ▼ ┌─────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┐ │ FOUNDATIONS │ SYSTEM IMPL │ INTEGRATION │ FRONTIER │ │ (Weeks 1-4) │ (Weeks 5-8) │ (Weeks 9-10) │ (Weeks 11-12) │ └─────┬───────┴──────┬───────┴──────┬───────┴─────────┬───────┘ │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ Math Models │ │ RAG Systems │ │ Multi-Agent │ │ Meta-Recurs │ │ Components │ │ Memory Arch │ │ Orchestrat │ │ Quantum Sem │ │ Processing │ │ Tool Integr │ │ Field Theory │ │ Self-Improv │ │ Management │ │ Agent Systems│ │ Evaluation │ │ Collaboration│ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ``` ## Why This Repository Exists > **"Meaning is not an intrinsic, static property of a semantic expression, but rather an emergent phenomenon" — [Agostino et al. — July 2025, Indiana University](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.10077)** Prompt engineering received all the attention, but we can now get excited for what comes next. Once you've mastered prompts, the real power comes from engineering the **entire context window** that surrounds those prompts. Guiding thought, if you will. This repository provides a progressive, first-principles approach to context engineering, built around a biological metaphor: ``` atoms → molecules → cells → organs → neural systems → neural & semantic field theory │ │ │ │ │ │ single few- memory + multi- cognitive tools + context = fields + prompt shot agents agents operating systems persistence & resonance ``` > "Abstraction is the cost of generalization"— [**Grant Sanderson (3Blue1Brown)**](https://www.3blue1brown.com/)
*[A Survey of Context Engineering - July 2025](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.13334)* **[On Emergence, Attractors, and Dynamical Systems Theory](https://content.csbs.utah.edu/~butner/systems/DynamicalSystemsIntro.html) | [Columbia DST](http://wordpress.ei.columbia.edu/ac4/about/our-approach/dynamical-systems-theory/)** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f046259-e5ec-4160-8ed0-41a608d8adf3 ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/309b8d8c-13b5-403c-9f1d-6a0ad551ea56)

[`00_foundations/01_atoms_prompting.md`](00_foundations/01_atoms_prompting.md)** (5 min) Understand why prompts alone often underperform 2. **Run [`10_guides_zero_to_hero/01_min_prompt.py`](10_guides_zero_to_hero/01_min_prompt.py)** (Jupyter Notebook style) Experiment with a minimal working example 3. **Explore [`20_templates/minimal_context.yaml`](20_templates/minimal_context.yaml)** Copy/paste a template into your own project 4. **Study [`30_examples/00_toy_chatbot/`](30_examples/00_toy_chatbot/)** See a complete implementation with context management ## Learning Path ``` ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌────────────────┐ │ 00_foundations/ │ │ 10_guides_zero_ │ │ 20_templates/ │ │ │────▶│ to_one/ │────▶│ │ │ Theory & core │ │ Hands-on │ │ Copy-paste │ │ concepts │ │ walkthroughs │ │ snippets │ └─────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌────────────────┐ │ 40_reference/ │◀───────────────────────────▶│ 30_examples/ │ │ │ │ │ │ Deep dives & │ │ Real projects, │ │ eval cookbook │ │ progressively │ └─────────────────┘ │ complex │ ▲ └────────────────┘ │ ▲ │ │ └────────────────────┐ ┌───────────┘ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────────┐ │ 50_contrib/ │ │ │ │ Community │ │ contributions │ └─────────────────────┘ ``` ## What You'll Learn | Concept | What It Is | Why It Matters | |---------|------------|----------------| | **Token Budget** | Optimizing every token in your context | More tokens = more $$ and slower responses | | **Few-Shot Learning** | Teaching by showing examples | Often works better than explanation alone | | **Memory Systems** | Persisting information across turns | Enables stateful, coherent interactions | | **Retrieval Augmentation** | Finding & injecting relevant documents | Grounds responses in facts, reduces hallucination | | **Control Flow** | Breaking complex tasks into steps | Solve harder problems with simpler prompts | | **Context Pruning** | Removing irrelevant information | Keep only what's necessary for performance | | **Metrics & Evaluation** | Measuring context effectiveness | Iterative optimization of token use vs. quality | | **Cognitive Tools & Prompt Programming** | Learm to build custom tools and templates | Prompt programming enables new layers for context engineering | | **Neural Field Theory** | Context as a Neural Field | Modeling context as a dynamic neural field allows for iterative context updating | | **Symbolic Mechanisms** | Symbolic architectures enable higher order reasoning | Smarter systems = less work | | **Quantum Semantics** | Meaning as observer-dependent | Design context systems leveraging superpositional techniques | ## Karpathy + 3Blue1Brown Inspired Style > For learners of all experience levels 1. **First principles** – start with the fundamental context 2. **Iterative add-on** – add only what the model demonstrably lacks 3. **Measure everything** – token cost, latency, quality score 4. **Delete ruthlessly** – pruning beats padding 5. **Code > slides** – every concept has a runnable cell 6. **Visualize everything** — every concept is visualized with ASCII and symbolic diagrams # Research Evidence ## Memory + Reasoning ### **[MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents - Singapore-MIT June 2025](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.15841)** > “Our results demonstrate the promise of reasoning-driven memory consolidation as a scalable alternative to existing solutions for training long-horizon interactive agents, where both efficiency and performance are optimized." — [Singapore-MIT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.15841) ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16e3f241-5f44-4ed5-9622-f0b4acbb67b0) 1. **MEM1 trains AI agents to keep only what matters—merging memory and reasoning at every step—so they never get overwhelmed, no matter how long the task.** 2. **Instead of piling up endless context, MEM1 compresses each interaction into a compact “internal state,” just like a smart note that gets updated, not recopied.** 3. **By blending memory and thinking into a single flow, MEM1 learns to remember only the essentials—making agents faster, sharper, and able to handle much longer conversations.** 4. **Everything the agent does is tagged and structured, so each action, question, or fact is clear and easy to audit—no more mystery meat memory.** 5. **With every cycle, old clutter is pruned and only the latest, most relevant insights are carried forward, mirroring how expert problem-solvers distill their notes.** 6. **MEM1 proves that recursive, protocol-driven memory—where you always refine and integrate—outperforms traditional “just add more context” approaches in both speed and accuracy.** ## Cognitive Tools ### **[Eliciting Reasoning in Language Models with Cognitive Tools - IBM Zurich June 2025](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.12115)** ### Prompts and Prompt Programs as Reasoning Tool Calls > “Cognitive tools” encapsulate reasoning operations within the LLM itself — [IBM Zurich](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.12115) ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd06c3f5-5a0b-4ee7-bbba-2f9f243f70ae) > **These cognitive tools (structured prompt templates as tool calls) break down the problem by identifying the main concepts at hand, extracting relevant information in the question, and highlighting meaningful properties, theorems, and techniques that might be helpful in solving the problem.** ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7ce8605-6fa3-494f-94cd-94e6b23032b6) > **These templates scaffold reasoning layers similar to cognitive mental shortcuts, commonly studied as "heuristics".** 1. **This research shows that breaking complex tasks into modular “cognitive tools” lets AI solve problems more thoughtfully—mirroring how expert humans reason step by step.** 2. **Instead of relying on a single, big prompt, the model calls specialized prompt templates, aka cognitive tools like “understand question,” “recall related,” “examine answer,” and “backtracking”—each handling a distinct mental operation.** 3. **Cognitive tools work like inner mental shortcuts: the AI picks the right program at each stage and runs it to plan its reasoning and downstream actions before conducting the task for greater accuracy and flexibility.** 4. **By compartmentalizing reasoning steps into modular blocks, these tools prevent confusion, reduce error, and make the model’s thought process transparent and auditable—even on hard math problems.** 5. **This modular approach upgrades both open and closed models—boosting real-world math problem-solving and approaching the performance of advanced RL-trained “reasoning” models, without extra training.** 6. **The results suggest that the seeds of powerful reasoning are already inside large language models—cognitive tools simply unlock and orchestrate these abilities, offering a transparent, efficient, and interpretable alternative to black-box tuning.** ## Emergent Symbols ## **[Emergent Symbolic Mechanisms Support Abstract Reasoning in Large Language Models - ICML Princeton June 18, 2025](https://openreview.net/forum?id=y1SnRPDWx4)** ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76c6e6cb-b65d-4af7-95a5-6d52aee7efc0) > **TL;DR: A three-stage architecture is identified that supports abstract reasoning in LLMs via a set of emergent symbol-processing mechanisms.** > > **These include symbolic induction heads, symbolic abstraction heads, and retrieval heads.** **1. In early layers, symbol abstraction heads convert input tokens to abstract variables based on the relations between those tokens.** **2. In intermediate layers, symbolic induction heads perform sequence induction over these abstract variables.** **3. Finally, in later layers, retrieval heads predict the next token by retrieving the value associated with the predicted abstract variable.** **These results point toward a resolution of the longstanding debate between symbolic and neural network approaches, suggesting that emergent reasoning in neural networks depends on the emergence of symbolic mechanisms.** — [**ICML Princeton**](https://openreview.net/forum?id=y1SnRPDWx4) ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2428544e-332a-4e32-9070-9f9d8716d491) > > **Why Useful?** > > > **This supports why Markdown, Json, and similar structured, symbolic formats are more easily LLM parsable** > > **Concept: Collaborate with agents to apply delimiters, syntax, symbols, symbolic words, metaphors and structure to improve reasoning/context/memory/persistence during inference** 1. **This paper proves that large language models develop their own inner symbolic “logic circuits”—enabling them to reason with abstract variables, not just surface word patterns.** 2. **LLMs show a three-stage process: first abstracting symbols from input, then reasoning over these variables, and finally mapping the abstract answer back to real-world tokens.** 3. **These emergent mechanisms mean LLMs don’t just memorize—they actually create internal, flexible representations that let them generalize to new problems and analogies.** 4. **Attention heads in early layers act like “symbol extractors,” intermediate heads perform symbolic reasoning, and late heads retrieve the concrete answer—mirroring human-like abstraction and retrieval.** 5. **By running targeted experiments and interventions, the authors show these symbolic processes are both necessary and sufficient for abstract reasoning, across multiple models and tasks.** 6. **The results bridge the historic gap between symbolic AI and neural nets—showing that, at scale, neural networks can invent and use symbolic machinery, supporting real generalization and reasoning.** ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=davidkimai/Context-Engineering&type=Date)](https://www.star-history.com/#davidkimai/Context-Engineering&Date) ## Contributing We welcome contributions! Check out [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines. ## License [MIT License](LICENSE) ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{context-engineering, author = {Context Engineering Contributors}, title = {Context Engineering: Beyond Prompt Engineering}, year = {2025}, publisher = {GitHub}, url = {https://github.com/davidkimai/context-engineering} } ``` ## Acknowledgements > I've been looking forward to this being conceptualized and formalized as there wasn't a prior established field. Prompt engineering receives quite the stigma and doesn't quite cover what most researchers and I do. - [Andrej Karpathy](https://x.com/karpathy/status/1937902205765607626) for coining "context engineering" and inspiring this repo - All contributors and the open source community

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Workspace Overview
     6→
     7→This is a home directory workspace containing multiple projects. It is **not** a single repository. Each major project has its own `CLAUDE.md` — always read the project-specific CLAUDE.md before working in that project.
     8→
     9→The global cognitive substrate instructions live at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and are always loaded automatically. This file covers **cross-project navigation and shared patterns**.
    10→
    11→## Project Map
    12→
    13→### Active Projects (with test commands)
    14→
    15→| Project | Path | Tests | Test Command |
    16→|---------|------|-------|-------------|
    17→| **Orchestra** v7.1.0 | `Orchestra/` | ~1,551 | `python -m pytest` |
    18→| **Synapse** v5.2.1 | `Synapse/` + `~/.synapse/` | ~973 | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    19→| **OTTO OS** v5.0.0-dev | `OTTO_OS/otto_v4/` | 93+4 | `cd otto_v4 && python -m pytest tests/ -v -m "not integration"` |
    20→| **OTTO Agents** v0.1.0 | `OTTO_OS/OTTO_Agents/` | — | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    21→| **comfyui-agent** v0.2.0 | `comfyui-agent/` | 134+ | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    22→| **RadiantSuite** | `RadiantSuite/` | 7 | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    23→| **Optimizer V8** | `Optimizer_V7_G3/` | — | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    24→| **RTXRemixCommandCenter** | `RTXRemixCommandCenter/` | — | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    25→| **vex-corpus** v0.1.0 | `vex-corpus/` | — | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    26→| **usd-security** v0.1.0 | `usd-security/` | — | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    27→| **Substrate Tools** | `~/.claude/substrate/tools/` | 293 | `python -m pytest tests/ -v` |
    28→
    29→### Shipped / Parked
    30→
    31→| Project | Path | Notes |
    32→|---------|------|-------|
    33→| **houdini-connector** | `houdini-connector/` | Shipped, C++/Python HDK plugin |
    34→| **usd-cognitive-substrate** | `usd-cognitive-substrate/` | Merged into Orchestra |
    35→| **cognitive-orchestrator** | `cognitive-orchestrator/` | Merged into Orchestra |
    36→| **persistent-state-hypothesis** | `persistent-state-hypothesis/` | Published paper (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18332346) |
    37→
    38→### Utilities (not full projects)
    39→
    40→- `dylan-fit-sync/` — Push running workouts to NordicTrack X24 via iFit
    41→- `career-check/` — Single-script career utility
    42→- `browser-test/` — Node.js browser testing (JavaScript)
    43→- `claude-code-mobile/` — Mobile workspace for GitHub @claude mentions
    44→- `comfyui-deterministic-toolkit/` — JetBlock deterministic ComfyUI workflows
    45→
    46→### Top-Level Scripts
    47→
    48→Dozens of one-off VFX Python scripts (`check_*.py`, `fix_*.py`, `setup_*.py`, `configure_*.py`) for Houdini/USD tasks. These are standalone — no shared module.
    49→
    50→## Cross-Project Patterns
    51→
    52→### He2025 Determinism
    53→
    54→All major projects follow ThinkingMachines [He2025] patterns for defeating nondeterminism:
    55→- `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization
    56→- Sorted dict iterations before aggregation
    57→- Stable tiebreakers (no `uuid.uuid4()` in hot paths, use deterministic IDs)
    58→- `time.time()` not used in seeds or hashing
    59→- Orchestra: `COGNITIVE_TILE_SIZE=32` + Kahan summation (batch invariance)
    60→
    61→### Testing
    62→
    63→- All Python projects use **pytest** (no unittest)
    64→- Orchestra uses `pytest.ini` (not pyproject.toml for pytest config); has `asyncio_mode=auto`
    65→- `--timeout` flag unavailable (pytest-timeout not installed)
    66→- Python 3.14 gotcha: `asyncio.get_event_loop()` raises RuntimeError — use `@pytest.mark.asyncio`
    67→- Orchestra CI excludes: `test_integration.py`, `test_performance.py`, `test_chaos.py`
    68→
    69→### Installation Pattern
    70→
    71→All major projects: `pip install -e ".[dev]"` for development. Optional features via extras (e.g., `".[dev,websocket,mcp]"`).
    72→
    73→### Windows Gotchas
    74→
    75→- **Encoding**: Use ASCII arrows (`<-`) not Unicode — cp1252 breaks in many contexts
    76→- **Imports for mocking**: `httpx`, `websockets` must be module-level for `mock.patch` to work
    77→- **Platform**: Windows, AMD Threadripper PRO 7965WX (24C/48T), RTX 4090 (24GB), 128GB DDR5
    78→
    79→## Shared Infrastructure
    80→
    81→### `~/.claude/` — Global Config
    82→
    83→- `CLAUDE.md` — Cognitive substrate instructions (always auto-loaded)
    84→- `substrate/tools/` — Substrate tool suite (293 tests, 86% coverage)
    85→- `substrate/knowledge/` — Knowledge prims (89 prims, 340+ triggers)
    86→- `projects/_index.md` — Project orchestration (FOCUS/HOLDING/PARKED status)
    87→- `session_state.json` — Cross-session state tracking
    88→
    89→### `~/.synapse/` — Synapse Companion
    90→
    91→- `agent/` — Autonomous Agent SDK (`anthropic` 0.75.0, `ws://localhost:9999/synapse`)
    92→- `design/` — Complete design system (tokens, 21 SVGs, Qt styles)
    93→- `houdini/` — Shelf and panel integration for Houdini
    94→- `install.py` — Installer with `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--uninstall`
    95→
    96→### `~/.orchestra/` — Orchestra Runtime State
    97→
    98→- `bcm/` — BCM learning trails (2-hour decay half-life)
    99→- `state/` — Session state
   100→
   101→## Lighting Law (VFX — Never Violate)
   102→
   103→When working with any PBR renderer (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray):
   104→- **Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 or below** — never set intensity > 1
   105→- **Brightness controlled by EXPOSURE** (logarithmic, in stops)
   106→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference; 4:1 = 2.0 stops
   107→- USD exposure parm: `xn__inputsexposure_vya`, control: `xn__inputsexposure_control_wcb` = `"set"`
   108→
   109→## Key External Paths
   110→
   111→- **ComfyUI**: `G:\COMFYUI_Database` (note: `Custom_Nodes` with capital C, N)
   112→- **Houdini Projects**: `D:\HOUDINI_PROJECTS_2025\`
   113→- **Vercel Portfolio**: `G:\VERCEL_BACKUP\my-vercel-website\` (Next.js/React)
   114→- **AI Framework R&D**: `H:\My Drive\AI_Framework_RnD_2025\Frameworks` (parked)

content.content:
1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Orchestra is a cognitive safety layer for AI-assisted development (v7.1.0). It sits between the user and Claude Code, tracking energy, momentum, and burnout to adapt AI behavior to actual user capacity.
     8→
     9→**Core principle:** Same signals → Same routing → Same behavior (ThinkingMachines [He2025] batch-invariance)
    10→
    11→## Development Commands
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→# Install
    15→pip install -e ".[dev]"           # Dev dependencies
    16→pip install -e ".[dev,tui]"       # With TUI dashboard
    17→pip install -e ".[distillation]"  # With knowledge distillation
    18→
    19→# Test
    20→pytest                                    # All 1,494 tests
    21→pytest tests/test_cognitive_engine.py -v  # Single file
    22→pytest tests/test_cognitive_engine.py::test_routing_determinism -v  # Single test
    23→pytest -k "routing"                       # Tests matching pattern
    24→pytest -m unit                            # Fast, isolated tests
    25→pytest -m integration                     # Full workflow tests
    26→pytest -m chaos                           # Fault injection tests
    27→pytest -m performance                     # SLA verification
    28→pytest -m contracts                       # Contract and schema validation
    29→pytest tests/distillation/ -v             # Knowledge distillation (118 tests)
    30→pytest --cov=src/orchestra --cov-report=html  # Coverage report
    31→
    32→# Hook testing
    33→echo '{"user_prompt": "test"}' | python -m orchestra.hooks
    34→
    35→# Knowledge distillation pipeline
    36→python -m orchestra.substrate.knowledge.distillation.pipeline \
    37→    --corpus ./docs --output ./knowledge --model claude-sonnet-4-20250514
    38→python -m orchestra.substrate.knowledge.distillation.pipeline \
    39→    --corpus ./docs --output ./knowledge  # Resume from checkpoint
    40→
    41→# CLI
    42→orchestra                    # Launch TUI dashboard
    43→orchestra status             # Show cognitive state
    44→orchestra status --short     # Minimal status line
    45→orchestra set -b YELLOW      # Set burnout level
    46→orchestra set -e low         # Set energy level
    47→orchestra install-hook       # Install Claude Code integration
    48→orchestra init bash          # Get bash prompt config
    49→orchestra init zsh           # Get zsh prompt config
    50→
    51→# Lint (advisory in CI, not blocking)
    52→ruff check src/orchestra/    # Linting (matches CI target)
    53→mypy src/orchestra/ --ignore-missing-imports  # Type checking
    54→```
    55→
    56→## CI/CD
    57→
    58→Tests run on GitHub Actions across Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 on Ubuntu and Windows (6 test matrix jobs + lint + type-check). All tests must pass before merge. Ruff and mypy run with `continue-on-error: true` (advisory). CI skips `test_integration.py`, `test_performance.py`, and `test_chaos.py` (these run locally only). CI uses `-x` (fail-fast) flag. Coverage uploads to Codecov from ubuntu/3.11 only.
    59→
    60→## Architecture: 8-Phase NEXUS Pipeline
    61→
    62→Every message passes through this deterministic pipeline:
    63→
    64→```
    65→Phase 0:  RETRIEVE  → Knowledge check (fast path, can short-circuit)
    66→Phase 0b: CLASSIFY  → Determine source mode: LEARN | ACCESS | HYBRID
    67→Phase 0c: GROUND    → Oracle query if ACCESS/HYBRID mode
    68→Phase 1:  DETECT    → PRISM extracts signals (priority: emotional > grounding > mode > domain > task)
    69→Phase 2:  CASCADE   → Safety gates + ADHD_MoE + GROUNDING_MoE + BCM trail metadata
    70→Phase 3:  LOCK      → MAX3 bounded reflection + safety gating + BCM depth optimization
    71→Phase 4:  EXECUTE   → Claude generates with locked params → [EXEC:checksum|expert|paradigm|altitude|depth|source_mode]
    72→Phase 5:  UPDATE    → RC^+xi convergence tracking + BCM trail updates (queued, batch-invariant)
    73→```
    74→
    75→### Core Modules
    76→
    77→| Module | Purpose |
    78→|--------|---------|
    79→| `cognitive_orchestrator.py` | 8-Phase pipeline coordination (entry point) |
    80→| `prism_detector.py` | Signal extraction (emotional > grounding > mode > domain > task priority) |
    81→| `expert_router.py` | ADHD_MoE (7 experts) + GROUNDING_MoE (4 experts), fixed priority |
    82→| `grounding_bridge.py` | Grounding layer adapter - ACCESS/LEARN/HYBRID routing |
    83→| `parameter_locker.py` | MAX3 bounded reflection + ADHD safety gating + source_mode |
    84→| `bcm_trail.py` | BCM stigmergic learning (v7.0.0) - trail confidence |
    85→| `bcm_integration.py` | BCM pipeline adapter - plasticity triggers |
    86→| `convergence_tracker.py` | RC^+xi epistemic tension tracking |
    87→| `batch_invariance.py` | Kahan summation, fixed tile size, aggregation strategies (v7.1.0) |
    88→| `cognitive_state.py` | State persistence (37 core + 7 BCM + 18 batch = 62 fields) |
    89→| `framework_orchestrator.py` | 7-agent async task orchestrator (separate system, not the NEXUS pipeline) |
    90→
    91→### Two Orchestrators
    92→
    93→`CognitiveOrchestrator` and `FrameworkOrchestrator` are **different systems**:
    94→
    95→- **`CognitiveOrchestrator`** — The NEXUS pipeline. Processes signals → routes to experts → locks params. This is what the Claude Code hook calls via `cognitive_hook.py`.
    96→- **`FrameworkOrchestrator`** — A 7-agent async task orchestrator (ECHO, DomainIntelligence, MoE, WorldModeler, CodeGenerator, DeterminismGuard, SelfReflector) with filesystem-based state, circuit breakers, and agent coordination. Used for multi-agent workflows.
    97→
    98→When modifying "the orchestrator," confirm which one.
    99→
   100→### Expert Routing
   101→
   102→7 ADHD_MoE experts + 4 GROUNDING_MoE experts in **fixed priority order** — see `expert_router.py`. Priority order (Validator > Scaffolder > ... > Direct, OracleResolver > ... > AccessGatekeeper) is a determinism invariant. First match wins.
   103→
   104→**BCM constraint**: BCM trail confidence is metadata-only — it never changes routing order.
   105→
   106→### Safety Gating
   107→
   108→User state overrides requests—`energy=depleted` forces minimal thinking depth, `burnout=RED` forces minimal. Safety can reduce depth, never increase.
   109→
   110→## ThinkingMachines Compliance
   111→
   112→All code must maintain batch-invariance:
   113→
   114→1. **Fixed evaluation order** — Never reorder phases or priority lists
   115→2. **No dynamic algorithm switching** — Selection must be deterministic
   116→3. **Parameter locking** — Lock all params before generation
   117→4. **Reproducible checksums** — Same inputs → same EXEC anchor
   118→5. **Sorted iteration** — Always sort sets/dicts before iteration
   119→6. **Queued BCM updates** — Flushed AFTER processing, never during
   120→
   121→```python
   122→# Good: Fixed priority, explicit ordering
   123→EXPERT_PRIORITY = [Expert.VALIDATOR, Expert.SCAFFOLDER, ...]
   124→
   125→# Bad: Dynamic ordering violates batch-invariance
   126→experts = sorted(experts, key=lambda e: compute_priority(e, state))
   127→```
   128→
   129→## Substrate Subpackage
   130→
   131→`src/orchestra/substrate/` contains three subsystems extracted from the cognitive orchestrator:
   132→
   133→| Subpackage | Purpose |
   134→|------------|---------|
   135→| `substrate/knowledge/` | O(1) factual retrieval (`KnowledgeRetriever`), plus `distillation/` pipeline (18 modules) for LLM-based knowledge extraction |
   136→| `substrate/ewm/` | External Working Memory — session anchors, time beacons, project friction tracking |
   137→| `substrate/hardening/` | Graceful degradation, backup/restore, handoff documents, state file management |
   138→
   139→## MCP Subpackage
   140→
   141→`packages/orchestra-mcp/` is a separate MCP (Model Context Protocol) server package with its own `pyproject.toml`. Published independently via `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml`.
   142→
   143→## Environment Variables
   144→
   145→| Variable | Purpose |
   146→|----------|---------|
   147→| `FO_WORKSPACE` | Workspace directory |
   148→| `FO_AGENT_TIMEOUT` | Per-agent timeout (seconds) |
   149→| `FO_LOG_FORMAT` | `text` or `json` |
   150→| `FO_LOG_LEVEL` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` |
   151→
   152→## Key Paths
   153→
   154→```
   155→src/orchestra/hooks/cognitive_hook.py     # Claude Code integration entry point
   156→src/orchestra/bcm_trail.py                # BCM trail system (v7.0.0)
   157→src/orchestra/substrate/                  # Knowledge, EWM, hardening subsystems
   158→packages/orchestra-mcp/                   # MCP server (separate package)
   159→~/.orchestra/state/cognitive_state.json   # Runtime state (62 fields)
   160→~/.orchestra/bcm/trail_{session}.json     # BCM trail persistence
   161→~/.orchestra/config/orchestra.json        # User preferences
   162→```
   163→
   164→**Hook data flow:** Claude Code calls `python -m orchestra.hooks` → stdin `{"user_prompt": "..."}` → `CognitiveOrchestrator.process_message()` → stdout `{"systemMessage": "[EXEC:...]"}`. Empty prompt → empty JSON `{}`.
   165→
   166→**Critical for determinism:** `expert_router.py` — Expert selection must maintain FIXED priority order.
   167→
   168→## Adding New State Fields
   169→
   170→New fields on `CognitiveState` **must have dataclass defaults**. Old state files won't contain them — deserialization uses `get_resolved_value(key, default)` for graceful fallback. Tests pass (fresh state), production breaks (loaded state) if defaults are missing.
   171→
   172→## Adding New Experts
   173→
   174→1. Add to `Expert` enum in `expert_router.py` at correct priority position
   175→2. Add triggers in `EXPERT_TRIGGERS` dict
   176→3. Add to `EXPERT_PRIORITY` list at correct position
   177→4. Add determinism tests (same input → same routing)
   178→
   179→## Adding New Signal Categories
   180→
   181→Signal priority order (emotional > grounding > mode > domain > task > energy) is core specification. Changes require careful consideration. Modify `SignalCategory` enum, `SIGNAL_PATTERNS`, `SignalVector` dataclass, and `PRISMDetector.detect()`.
   182→
   183→## Anti-Patterns
   184→
   185→- **Never reorder** phase execution or priority lists
   186→- **Never use dynamic** algorithm switching at runtime
   187→- **Never skip** determinism tests for new features
   188→- **Never break** parameter locking before generation
   189→- **Never spawn agents** when burnout >= ORANGE (simplify instead)
   190→- **Never apply BCM updates** during processing (queue for FLUSH phase)
   191→- **Never remove** `conftest.py` module aliases (`sys.modules['framework_orchestrator']`, etc.) — these are intentional backward-compat shims that tests depend on
   192→

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Synapse v5.2.0 is an AI-Houdini Bridge — a standalone Python package (zero required dependencies) that lets AI assistants control SideFX Houdini via WebSocket. It exposes 43 MCP tools to Claude Desktop/Code for real-time scene manipulation, persistent project memory, adaptive tiered LLM routing, and viewport/render capture.
     8→
     9→Two repos make up the full system:
    10→- **`C:\Users\User\Synapse\`** — Core server, protocol, handlers, memory, routing, MCP bridge
    11→- **`C:\Users\User\.synapse\`** — Agent SDK (autonomous co-pilot), design system (tokens/icons/styles), Houdini shelf/panel integration, installer
    12→
    13→## Development Commands
    14→
    15→```bash
    16→# Install for development
    17→pip install -e ".[dev]"
    18→pip install -e ".[dev,websocket,mcp,routing,encryption]"   # all optional features
    19→
    20→# Run all core tests (~825 tests, no Houdini required)
    21→python -m pytest tests/ -v
    22→
    23→# Type checking (mypy, 0 errors on 49 source files)
    24→python -m mypy python/synapse/ --config-file pyproject.toml
    25→
    26→# Build API docs (MkDocs + mkdocstrings)
    27→python -m mkdocs build
    28→
    29→# Key test files
    30→python -m pytest tests/test_routing.py -v              # Routing cascade (~323 tests)
    31→python -m pytest tests/test_pipeline_efficiency.py -v   # RWLock, tier-pinning, batch, concurrent (35 tests)
    32→python -m pytest tests/test_materials.py -v             # Material tools (19 tests)
    33→python -m pytest tests/test_render.py -v                # Karma/Mantra pipeline
    34→python -m pytest tests/test_introspection.py -v         # Scene inspection
    35→python -m pytest tests/test_core.py -v                  # Determinism, audit, gates
    36→python -m pytest tests/test_agent.py -v                 # Agent protocol, executor
    37→python -m pytest tests/test_resilience.py -v            # Rate limiter, circuit breaker
    38→python -m pytest tests/test_auth.py -v                  # Authentication (21 tests)
    39→python -m pytest tests/test_stress.py -v                # Load/stress testing (24 tests)
    40→python -m pytest tests/test_integration_pipeline.py -v  # Integration pipeline (20 tests)
    41→python -m pytest tests/test_sqlite_store.py -v          # SQLite memory backend (40 tests)
    42→
    43→# Single test
    44→python -m pytest tests/test_routing.py::test_routing_benchmark -v
    45→
    46→# Agent SDK tests (from .synapse/agent/)
    47→python -m pytest C:\Users\User\.synapse\agent\tests\ -v    # 49 tests
    48→
    49→# Design system tests (from .synapse/)
    50→python -m pytest C:\Users\User\.synapse\tests\test_design_system.py -v   # 44 tests
    51→
    52→# Coverage
    53→python -m pytest tests/ --cov=synapse --cov-report=term-missing
    54→```
    55→
    56→**CI**: GitHub Actions on Python 3.11 + 3.14, runs `python -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short`.
    57→
    58→## Architecture
    59→
    60→### Data Flow (MCP to Houdini)
    61→
    62→```
    63→Claude Desktop/Code
    64→    |  stdio / JSON-RPC
    65→mcp_server.py  (43 tools, concurrent dispatch via _pending dict + _recv_loop)
    66→    |  WebSocket: ws://localhost:9999/synapse
    67→SynapseServer  (daemon thread inside Houdini)
    68→    |  CommandHandlerRegistry (handlers.py)
    69→hou.* Python API
    70→    |
    71→Houdini USD Stage / Solaris / Karma
    72→```
    73→
    74→### Core Package Layout (`python/synapse/`)
    75→
    76→| Layer | Directory | Responsibility |
    77→|-------|-----------|---------------|
    78→| Foundation | `core/` | Wire protocol (`protocol.py`), parameter aliases (`aliases.py`), determinism (`determinism.py`), audit chain (`audit.py`), human gates (`gates.py`), encryption (`crypto.py`), command queue (`queue.py`) |
    79→| Memory | `memory/` | JSONL store (`store.py`) or SQLite store (`sqlite_store.py`, via `SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND=sqlite`), data models (`models.py`), shot context (`context.py`), markdown export (`markdown.py`), **Living Memory**: scene memory (`scene_memory.py`), agent state USD (`agent_state.py`), evolution system (`evolution.py`) |
    80→| Routing | `routing/` | Tiered LLM dispatch (`router.py`), regex parser (`parser.py`), RAG knowledge (`knowledge.py`), recipes (`recipes.py`), deterministic cache (`cache.py`), workflow planner (`planner.py`), epoch-based tier adaptation (`adaptation.py`) |
    81→| Agent | `agent/` | prepare/propose/execute/learn lifecycle (`executor.py`), task/plan/step protocol (`protocol.py`), outcome tracking (`learning.py`) |
    82→| Server | `server/` | WebSocket server (`websocket.py`), 39 command handlers (`handlers.py`), resilience stack (`resilience.py`), scene introspection (`introspection.py`), hwebserver adapter (`hwebserver_adapter.py`), REST adapter (`api_adapter.py`), guard functions (`guards.py`), authentication (`auth.py`), Prometheus metrics (`metrics.py`) |
    83→| Session | `session/` | SynapseBridge singleton hub (`tracker.py`), session summaries (`summary.py`) |
    84→| UI | `ui/` | Qt panel with 5 tabs (`panel.py`), tab widgets in `tabs/` |
    85→
    86→### Routing Cascade (cheapest-first)
    87→
    88→```
    89→Cache(O(1)) -> Recipe(O(1)) -> Planner(O(1)) -> Tier0/regex(O(n)) -> Tier1/RAG(O(log n)) -> Tier2/Haiku(~5s) -> Tier3/Agent(~15s)
    90→```
    91→
    92→- **Tier pinning** (He2025 consistency): Same input+context maps to same tier on subsequent calls. LRU cache, max 1,000 pins, stale pins fall through.
    93→- **Speculative T0+T1 parallelism**: Module-level `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` runs Tier 0 regex and Tier 1 knowledge lookup concurrently.
    94→- **Tier 1 result threading**: `route()` runs `knowledge.lookup()` once, threads the result to all higher tiers to avoid redundant lookups.
    95→
    96→### Transport Backends
    97→
    98→| Backend | Module | Latency | Use Case |
    99→|---------|--------|---------|----------|
   100→| `websockets` | `server/websocket.py` | ~0.2ms warm ping | Primary — reads, pings, everything |
   101→| `hwebserver` | `server/hwebserver_adapter.py` | ~2s floor (main event loop) | Optional — only for hou.* mutations |
   102→
   103→Both share the same handler layer. Decision: websockets is primary; hwebserver's 2s floor per message outweighs its benefits.
   104→
   105→### Authentication (`server/auth.py`)
   106→
   107→Optional API key authentication for both transports. Key sources (checked in order):
   108→1. `SYNAPSE_API_KEY` environment variable
   109→2. `~/.synapse/auth.key` file (first non-empty, non-comment line)
   110→3. No key configured -> auth disabled (backward compat)
   111→
   112→When enabled, first WebSocket message must be an `authenticate` command with `{"payload": {"key": "..."}}`. Uses `hmac.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison. Auth handshake integrated into both `websocket.py` and `hwebserver_adapter.py`.
   113→
   114→### MCP Server (`mcp_server.py`)
   115→
   116→38 tools. Key operational details:
   117→- **Concurrent dispatch**: `_pending` dict + `_recv_loop` coroutine — no blocking lock, true parallel tool calls
   118→- **Timeouts**: Default 10s. Overrides: execute_python/execute_vex/capture_viewport/inspect_* at 30s, render/wedge at 120s, batch at 60s
   119→- **JSON**: Uses `orjson` (fast, sort_keys via `OPT_SORT_KEYS`) when available, falls back to stdlib `json`
   120→- **Warmup**: Pre-connect in `main()` reduces first-call latency
   121→- **Retry**: `MAX_RETRIES=2`, `RETRY_DELAY=0.3`, auto-retry on connection drop
   122→- **Connection**: `open_timeout=3.0`, `ping_interval=None`, `compression=None` (localhost optimization)
   123→
   124→### `.synapse` Companion Repos
   125→
   126→**Agent SDK** (`~/.synapse/agent/`): Autonomous VFX co-pilot powered by Claude Opus 4.6. Standard Anthropic tool-use message loop (NOT a separate agent framework). 8 tools via direct WebSocket to Synapse. Safety: atomic mutations, idempotent guards, undo-group rollback. 49 tests.
   127→
   128→**Design System** (`~/.synapse/design/`): Pentagram-style monochromatic design. `tokens.py` (colors, typography, spacing — stdlib-only), `generate_icons.py` (21 SVGs from construction rules), `synapse_styles.py` (Qt stylesheet generator). Primary accent: SIGNAL cyan `#00D4FF`.
   129→
   130→**Houdini Integration** (`~/.synapse/houdini/`): `synapse.shelf` (5 toolbar tools), `synapse_shelf.py` (shelf callbacks — inspect, health check, docs), `synapse_panel.pypanel` (PySide2 panel with status polling).
   131→
   132→**Installer** (`~/.synapse/install.py`): Auto-detects Houdini prefs dir, copies shelf/panel/icons. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--uninstall`.
   133→
   134→## Testing Patterns
   135→
   136→**No Houdini required**: All tests import modules via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, bypassing the `hou` dependency. There is no shared `conftest.py` — each test file creates its own minimal `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules["hou"] = mock_hou`. Some test files (e.g., `test_guards.py`, `test_keyframe_aov.py`) save and restore the original `sys.modules["hou"]` in teardown to prevent cross-test pollution.
   137→
   138→**Patching `hou` in handler tests**: Always patch the module-level reference inside handlers.py, NOT `sys.modules["hou"]`. Patching sys.modules breaks object identity across test files.
   139→
   140→```python
   141→# Correct — patch the handlers module's hou reference
   142→_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou
   143→with patch.object(_handlers_hou, "node", return_value=mock_node):
   144→    ...
   145→
   146→# For attributes missing from the stub
   147→with patch.object(hou, "flipbook", create=True):
   148→    ...
   149→```
   150→
   151→**test_guards.py ordering**: Replaces `sys.modules["hou"]` entirely — has save/restore teardown to prevent pollution. `test_render.py` captures `_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou` to patch the correct object.
   152→
   153→**Error assertions**: Use `"Couldn't find"` (not `"not found"`) — matches coaching tone convention.
   154→
   155→**Windows encoding**: Any test writing files with em-dashes or special chars must use `encoding="utf-8"` (cp1252 breaks).
   156→
   157→## Adding New Functionality
   158→
   159→### Adding a new MCP tool
   160→
   161→1. Add `CommandType` variant in `core/protocol.py`
   162→2. Add handler method `_handle_<name>` in `server/handlers.py` and register it in `SynapseHandler._register_handlers()`
   163→3. Add parameter aliases in `core/aliases.py` if the tool has new parameter names
   164→4. Add `Tool(...)` entry to `list_tools()` and dispatch case to `call_tool()` in `mcp_server.py` (uses `Server.list_tools()`/`Server.call_tool()` decorators, not `@mcp.tool()`)
   165→5. Add timeout override to `_SLOW_COMMANDS` in `mcp_server.py` if >10s expected
   166→6. Write tests — bootstrap a `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules`, import handlers via `importlib`, patch `_handlers_hou` (not `sys.modules["hou"]`)
   167→
   168→### Adding a routing recipe
   169→
   170→Add to `routing/recipes.py` in the `_register_builtins()` method. 21 recipes (11 basic + 10 production). Recipes are Tier 0.5 — pattern-matched before regex, return multi-step command sequences. For complex workflows, use `execute_python` steps. For dynamic composition with modifiers ("set up X with Y and Z"), add workflow templates to `routing/planner.py`.
   171→
   172→### Adding RAG knowledge
   173→
   174→Add/edit files in `rag/skills/houdini21-reference/*.md` (26 files, ~3,900 lines). Update topic triggers in `rag/documentation/_metadata/semantic_index.json` (28 topics, 400+ triggers).
   175→
   176→## Key Conventions
   177→
   178→**Coaching tone**: Error messages say "Couldn't find node" not "Node not found". Always offer next step. `_suggest_parms(node, name)` provides substring-matched alternatives. See `TONE.md` for the full voice guide.
   179→
   180→**He2025 determinism**: `round_float()` for OUTPUT only — never internal timing. `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization (both stdlib `json.dumps` and `orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS`). `@deterministic` decorator auto-rounds float args. `kahan_sum()` for stable aggregation. Content-based UUIDs via `deterministic_uuid()`. Epoch-based adaptation uses fixed epoch SIZE (not time-based) per He2025.
   181→
   182→**Lazy loading**: `__init__.py` uses `__getattr__` to defer routing/server/UI imports. Optional deps use try/except with `*_AVAILABLE` flags. Keeps Houdini startup fast.
   183→
   184→**Thread safety**: `ReadWriteLock` (writer-priority) in `MemoryStore`. `threading.Lock()` for tier-pin cache. `threading.Event()` for background store loading. `_log_executor` ThreadPoolExecutor(2) for fire-and-forget memory logging.
   185→
   186→**Backwards compat**: All legacy names preserved — `NexusServer`, `EngramMemory`, `HyphaeAuditLog`, etc. Storage auto-migrates from `.nexus/`/`.engram/` to `.synapse/`.
   187→
   188→**Singletons**: `AuditLog`, `HumanGate`, `SynapseBridge`, `CryptoEngine` — accessed via `audit_log()`, `human_gate()`, `get_bridge()`, `get_crypto()`.
   189→
   190→**Error classification**: User errors (`ValueError`, `KeyError`, `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `IndexError`, `NameError`) do NOT trip circuit breaker. Service errors (`TimeoutError`, threading errors, Houdini crashes) DO trip it.
   191→
   192→**Rollback errors in execute_python**: `_ROLLBACK_ERRORS = (NameError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError, IndexError)` trigger auto-undo. Operational errors (RuntimeError, hou.OperationFailed) do NOT — earlier mutations may be valid.
   193→
   194→## Lighting Law (Critical Domain Knowledge)
   195→
   196→**Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 (or below)**. Brightness is controlled by **exposure** (logarithmic, in stops). This applies to ALL PBR renderers (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray).
   197→
   198→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference (`log2(3)`)
   199→- Key:fill ratio 4:1 = 2.0 stops difference (`log2(4)`)
   200→- USD exposure parm: `xn__inputsexposure_vya` (value), `xn__inputsexposure_control_wcb` = `"set"` (enable)
   201→- USD intensity parm: `xn__inputsintensity_i0a` — always 1.0
   202→
   203→## Wire Protocol
   204→
   205→Default: `ws://localhost:9999/synapse` | Version: `4.0.0`
   206→
   207→39 registered handlers: `ping`, `get_health`, `get_help`, `create_node`, `delete_node`, `connect_nodes`, `get_parm`, `set_parm`, `get_scene_info`, `get_selection`, `execute_python`, `execute_vex`, `get_stage_info`, `get_usd_attribute`, `set_usd_attribute`, `create_usd_prim`, `modify_usd_prim`, `capture_viewport`, `render`, `wedge`, `reference_usd`, `set_keyframe`, `render_settings`, `create_material`, `assign_material`, `read_material`, `knowledge_lookup`, `inspect_selection`, `inspect_scene`, `inspect_node`, `batch_commands`, `get_metrics`, `router_stats`, `list_recipes`, `context`, `search`, `add_memory`, `decide`, `recall`
   208→
   209→Parameter names resolve through `aliases.py` (38+ mappings) — e.g., `node`, `path`, `node_path` all resolve to canonical `node`.
   210→
   211→## Storage Layout
   212→
   213→```
   214→$HIP/.synapse/           # Per-project memory
   215→  memory.jsonl           # Append-only log (async write buffer: 2s flush / 50-item cap / atexit flush)
   216→  index.json             # Search indices (by_type, by_tag, by_keyword)
   217→  context.md             # Human-editable shot context
   218→  decisions.md           # Decision log
   219→  tasks.md               # Task history
   220→
   221→~/.synapse/              # Global
   222→  audit/                 # Daily JSONL audit logs (hash-chain, tamper-evident)
   223→  gates/                 # Gate proposals (timestamped, immutable)
   224→  encryption.key         # Auto-generated Fernet key (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256)
   225→  agent/                 # Autonomous agent SDK (synapse_agent.py entry point)
   226→  design/                # Design tokens, icon generator, Qt styles
   227→  houdini/               # Shelf, panel, callbacks for Houdini integration
   228→  install.py             # Houdini prefs installer
   229→```
   230→
   231→## Gotchas
   232→
   233→- **matlib.cook(force=True)**: MUST cook materiallibrary before `createNode()` on shader child — without cook, internal subnet doesn't exist and createNode returns None
   234→- **Render output_file kwarg**: Doesn't work for usdrender ROPs — set `outputimage` or `picture` parm directly
   235→- **usdrender loppath**: ROPs in `/out` need `loppath` set to a LOP node — handler auto-discovers display node in `/stage`
   236→- **Karma camera**: Must use USD prim path (`/cameras/render_cam`), not Houdini node path
   237→- **override_res**: String menu `""` / `"scale"` / `"specific"` — not int
   238→- **Viewport capture**: Must use Flipbook API with `hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult()` — `QWidget.grab()` returns black for OpenGL; `executeDeferred()` is fire-and-forget and won't block
   239→- **.pypanel imports**: NEVER nuke `sys.modules` — use `hou.session` guard for one-time import
   240→- **RAG Path import**: Handler uses `from pathlib import Path as _Path` (inline) — global `Path` not available in handlers.py
   241→- **MCP execute_python**: MCP param is `code`, but Synapse handler resolves `content` — payload builder in mcp_server.py maps it
   242→- **SVG icon generation**: XML forbids `--` inside comments; use `|` separator
   243→- **synapse_shelf.py**: Security hooks block `parm.eval()` patterns; use `node.evalParm("parm_name")` method instead
   244→- **Agent SDK websockets**: Must import at module level (not inside connect()) — patch target is `synapse_ws.websockets`
   245→- **Zombie servers**: Multiple SynapseServer instances can linger in Houdini; use `gc.get_objects()` + `_actual_port` to find the active one
   246→- **MCP tool registration**: Uses `@server.list_tools()` returning `Tool(...)` list + `@server.call_tool()` dispatcher — NOT the `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern. All 38 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   247→- **SYNAPSE_PATH env var**: Controls WebSocket path segment (default `/synapse`). `SYNAPSE_PORT` controls port (default `9999`). Full URL: `ws://localhost:{SYNAPSE_PORT}{SYNAPSE_PATH}`
   248→- **orjson optional**: `protocol.py` and `mcp_server.py` use `orjson` for fast JSON with `OPT_SORT_KEYS` when installed, auto-fallback to stdlib `json`
   249→

1→# SYNAPSE SAFE EXECUTION — Claude Code Implementation Brief
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→You are modifying **Synapse**, a WebSocket bridge between Claude (AI) and SideFX Houdini 21.
     6→Synapse runs as a Python server inside Houdini, receiving JSON commands over `ws://localhost:9999`
     7→and executing them in Houdini's Python environment (with full `hou` module access).
     8→
     9→### The Problem We're Solving
    10→
    11→When Claude sends Python code via `houdini_execute_python`, the code executes line-by-line
    12→inside Houdini. If the script errors on line 15, lines 1-14 have already mutated scene state
    13→(created nodes, connected wires, changed parameters). Synapse reports "error" but doesn't
    14→indicate which lines succeeded. When Claude retries, duplicate nodes/connections are created.
    15→
    16→**Real example that caused this:** A single script that (1) wired two lights into a merge node,
    17→then (2) inspected material parameters. Step 2 errored on a variable name bug. Claude retried
    18→the whole script. Lights got wired 3x into the same merge. The merge had 10 inputs instead of 6.
    19→
    20→### What We're Building
    21→
    22→Three-layer safety system:
    23→
    24→| Layer | What | Where |
    25→|-------|------|-------|
    26→| 1. Atomic | One mutation per call convention | Claude behavior (already saved to memory) |
    27→| 2. Idempotent Guards | Helper functions that check-before-mutate | `guards.py` module |
    28→| 3. Transaction Wrapper | Auto undo-group around all execute_python calls | Server handler modification |
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→## Step 0: Locate the Synapse Source
    33→
    34→The Synapse server source is likely in one of these locations:
    35→- C:/Users/User/.synapse/
    36→- C:/Users/User/Documents/synapse/
    37→- C:/Users/User/OneDrive/Documents/houdini_shared_tools/synapse/
    38→
    39→Search for the file that contains the `houdini_execute_python` handler. It will have code
    40→resembling `exec(code, namespace)` and `namespace.get('result')`.
    41→
    42→**Important:** Read the full server source before making changes. Understand:
    43→- How the WebSocket handler dispatches commands
    44→- How `houdini_execute_python` currently works
    45→- What namespace/globals are passed to `exec()`
    46→- How errors are currently caught and reported
    47→- Whether there's already any undo integration
    48→
    49→---
    50→
    51→## Step 1: Implement `guards.py` (Idempotent Helpers)
    52→
    53→Create `guards.py` in Synapse's Python module path. This module will be auto-imported
    54→into the execution namespace (see Step 2) so Claude's scripts can use these functions
    55→without explicit imports.
    56→
    57→### guards.py — Full Implementation
    58→
    59→```python
    60→"""
    61→guards.py — Synapse Idempotent Operation Guards
    62→
    63→These functions check scene state before mutating, making every operation
    64→safe to re-run. If the desired state already exists, they no-op and return
    65→the existing object/True.
    66→
    67→Usage (from any Synapse-executed script):
    68→    node = ensure_node('/stage', 'distantlight::2.0', 'rim_light')
    69→    ensure_connection('/stage/rim_light', '/stage/scene_merge')
    70→    ensure_parm('/stage/rim_light', 'xn__inputsintensity_i0a', 5.0)
    71→"""
    72→
    73→import hou
    74→from typing import Optional, Union
    75→
    76→
    77→def ensure_node(parent_path, node_type, node_name):
    78→    """Create node only if it doesn't already exist. Returns the node."""
    79→    full_path = f"{parent_path}/{node_name}"
    80→    existing = hou.node(full_path)
    81→    if existing is not None:
    82→        return existing
    83→    parent = hou.node(parent_path)
    84→    if parent is None:
    85→        raise ValueError(f"Parent node not found: {parent_path}")
    86→    return parent.createNode(node_type, node_name)
    87→
    88→
    89→def ensure_node_deleted(node_path):
    90→    """Delete node only if it exists. Returns True if deleted or already gone."""
    91→    node = hou.node(node_path)
    92→    if node is None:
    93→        return True
    94→    node.destroy()
    95→    return True
    96→
    97→
    98→def node_exists(path):
    99→    """Check if a node exists at the given path."""
   100→    return hou.node(path) is not None
   101→
   102→
   103→def ensure_connection(source_path, target_path, source_output=0, target_input=None):
   104→    """
   105→    Connect source to target only if not already connected.
   106→    If target_input is None, appends to next available input index.
   107→    Returns True if connection exists (whether new or pre-existing).
   108→    """
   109→    source = hou.node(source_path)
   110→    target = hou.node(target_path)
   111→    if not source or not target:
   112→        raise ValueError(f"Node not found: {source_path if not source else target_path}")
   113→    existing_inputs = target.inputs()
   114→    for idx, inp in enumerate(existing_inputs):
   115→        if inp and inp.path() == source.path():
   116→            return True
   117→    if target_input is not None:
   118→        target.setInput(target_input, source, source_output)
   119→    else:
   120→        next_idx = len(existing_inputs)
   121→        target.setInput(next_idx, source, source_output)
   122→    return True
   123→
   124→
   125→def ensure_disconnected(target_path, source_path):
   126→    """Disconnect source from target's inputs. Removes ALL connections from source to target."""
   127→    target = hou.node(target_path)
   128→    if not target:
   129→        return True
   130→    inputs = target.inputs()
   131→    for idx in range(len(inputs) - 1, -1, -1):
   132→        inp = inputs[idx]
   133→        if inp and inp.path() == source_path:
   134→            target.setInput(idx, None)
   135→    return True
   136→
   137→
   138→def deduplicate_inputs(merge_path):
   139→    """Remove duplicate connections on a merge node. Returns report dict."""
   140→    merge = hou.node(merge_path)
   141→    if not merge:
   142→        raise ValueError(f"Node not found: {merge_path}")
   143→    seen = set()
   144→    to_disconnect = []
   145→    inputs = merge.inputs()
   146→    for idx, inp in enumerate(inputs):
   147→        if inp is None:
   148→            continue
   149→        if inp.path() in seen:
   150→            to_disconnect.append(idx)
   151→        else:
   152→            seen.add(inp.path())
   153→    for idx in reversed(to_disconnect):
   154→        merge.setInput(idx, None)
   155→    return {'removed': len(to_disconnect), 'remaining': list(seen)}
   156→
   157→
   158→def ensure_parm(node_path, parm_name, value):
   159→    """Set parameter only if current value differs. Returns True on success."""
   160→    node = hou.node(node_path)
   161→    if not node:
   162→        raise ValueError(f"Node not found: {node_path}")
   163→    parm = node.parm(parm_name)
   164→    if not parm:
   165→        raise ValueError(f"Parameter not found: {node_path}/{parm_name}")
   166→    current = parm.eval()
   167→    if isinstance(value, float):
   168→        if abs(current - value) < 1e-7:
   169→            return True
   170→    elif current == value:
   171→        return True
   172→    parm.set(value)
   173→    return True
   174→
   175→
   176→def ensure_parm_tuple(node_path, parm_names, values):
   177→    """Set multiple related parameters (e.g. color rgb). Only sets if any differ."""
   178→    node = hou.node(node_path)
   179→    if not node:
   180→        raise ValueError(f"Node not found: {node_path}")
   181→    needs_update = False
   182→    for parm_name, value in zip(parm_names, values):
   183→        parm = node.parm(parm_name)
   184→        if not parm:
   185→            continue
   186→        current = parm.eval()
   187→        if isinstance(value, float):
   188→            if abs(current - value) > 1e-7:
   189→                needs_update = True
   190→                break
   191→        elif current != value:
   192→            needs_update = True
   193→            break
   194→    if not needs_update:
   195→        return True
   196→    for parm_name, value in zip(parm_names, values):
   197→        parm = node.parm(parm_name)
   198→        if parm:
   199→            parm.set(value)
   200→    return True
   201→
   202→
   203→def describe_inputs(node_path):
   204→    """Return list of input connection paths for a node."""
   205→    node = hou.node(node_path)
   206→    if not node:
   207→        return []
   208→    return [inp.path() if inp else None for inp in node.inputs()]
   209→
   210→
   211→def describe_node(node_path):
   212→    """Return basic info about a node."""
   213→    node = hou.node(node_path)
   214→    if not node:
   215→        return {'exists': False}
   216→    return {
   217→        'exists': True,
   218→        'path': node.path(),
   219→        'type': node.type().name(),
   220→        'inputs': len([i for i in node.inputs() if i]),
   221→        'outputs': len(node.outputs()),
   222→    }
   223→```
   224→
   225→---
   226→
   227→## Step 2: Implement Transaction Wrapper (Server Handler Modification)
   228→
   229→Find the `houdini_execute_python` handler in the Synapse server source.
   230→Modify it to wrap in an undo group with rollback on error:
   231→
   232→```python
   233→# AFTER (with transaction safety)
   234→import guards
   235→
   236→def handle_execute_python(code):
   237→    namespace = {
   238→        "hou": hou,
   239→        # Auto-inject guards so scripts don't need to import them
   240→        "ensure_node": guards.ensure_node,
   241→        "ensure_connection": guards.ensure_connection,
   242→        "ensure_disconnected": guards.ensure_disconnected,
   243→        "ensure_parm": guards.ensure_parm,
   244→        "ensure_parm_tuple": guards.ensure_parm_tuple,
   245→        "ensure_node_deleted": guards.ensure_node_deleted,
   246→        "node_exists": guards.node_exists,
   247→        "deduplicate_inputs": guards.deduplicate_inputs,
   248→        "describe_inputs": guards.describe_inputs,
   249→        "describe_node": guards.describe_node,
   250→    }
   251→    
   252→    with hou.undos.group("synapse_operation"):
   253→        try:
   254→            exec(code, namespace)
   255→            return {
   256→                "result": namespace.get("result"),
   257→                "executed": True
   258→            }
   259→        except Exception as e:
   260→            hou.undos.performUndo()
   261→            raise e
   262→```
   263→
   264→### Critical Implementation Notes:
   265→
   266→1. **Import guards at server startup**, not per-call
   267→2. **Preserve existing namespace items** — only ADD guard functions to existing namespace
   268→3. **Add fallback** if `hou.undos.group()` isn't available:
   269→   ```python
   270→   try:
   271→       with hou.undos.group("synapse_operation"):
   272→           exec(code, namespace)
   273→   except AttributeError:
   274→       exec(code, namespace)  # fallback without undo
   275→   ```
   276→4. **The error re-raise is critical** — after undo, error must still propagate to Claude
   277→5. **Add guards.py to Python path** if not auto-discoverable:
   278→   ```python
   279→   import sys, os
   280→   sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
   281→   import guards
   282→   ```
   283→
   284→---
   285→
   286→## Step 3: Test Protocol
   287→
   288→Run these against the **live Houdini scene** (Synapse at ws://localhost:9999).
   289→Scene: `synapse_demo_2026.hip`, nodes at `/stage/`.
   290→
   291→### Test 1: Idempotent Node Creation
   292→```python
   293→node = ensure_node('/stage', 'null', 'safety_test_null')
   294→result = f"Node: {node.path()}"
   295→```
   296→Run TWICE. Expected: Same path returned both times. Only one node exists.
   297→
   298→### Test 2: Idempotent Connection
   299→```python
   300→ensure_node('/stage', 'null', 'safety_test_null')
   301→ensure_connection('/stage/safety_test_null', '/stage/scene_merge')
   302→result = describe_inputs('/stage/scene_merge')
   303→```
   304→Run TWICE. Expected: safety_test_null appears exactly once in merge inputs.
   305→
   306→### Test 3: Transaction Rollback
   307→```python
   308→node = ensure_node('/stage', 'null', 'rollback_test')
   309→x = undefined_variable_that_will_crash
   310→```
   311→Expected: Error reported. `/stage/rollback_test` does NOT exist (undo rolled it back).
   312→
   313→### Test 4: Parameter Idempotency
   314→```python
   315→ensure_parm('/stage/hero_sphere', 'radius', 1.0)
   316→result = "Parm set (no-op if already 1.0)"
   317→```
   318→
   319→### Test 5: Cleanup
   320→```python
   321→ensure_node_deleted('/stage/safety_test_null')
   322→ensure_node_deleted('/stage/rollback_test')
   323→result = "Cleaned up"
   324→```
   325→
   326→---
   327→
   328→## Architecture Note
   329→
   330→This is intentionally lightweight. We're NOT building:
   331→- A full ORM for Houdini's node graph
   332→- A command queue or replay system
   333→- Persistent operation logging
   334→
   335→We ARE building:
   336→- Defensive helpers that make re-runs safe
   337→- An undo safety net that prevents partial-mutation corruption
   338→- Functions auto-injected into Claude's execution namespace
   339→
   340→**The goal: Claude can be sloppy and nothing breaks.**

1→# SYNAPSE — VFX Co-Pilot
     2→
     3→## Identity
     4→
     5→You are Synapse, a VFX co-pilot that works alongside professional artists
     6→in SideFX Houdini 21. You have direct access to their live scene through
     7→custom tools. You're not a chatbot — you're a creative collaborator with
     8→the ability to inspect, build, and verify VFX work in real time.
     9→
    10→## Voice & Tone
    11→
    12→**You sound like a supportive senior artist who has the artist's back.**
    13→
    14→### The Validation Test
    15→Before sending any message, ask yourself:
    16→> "Would this message make an artist having a rough day want to keep going
    17→>  or close the application?"
    18→
    19→If the answer isn't clearly "keep going," rewrite it.
    20→
    21→### Communication Principles
    22→- **Never blame.** "I couldn't find" not "you gave me a wrong path"
    23→- **Plain language first.** Technical details can follow, not lead
    24→- **Always offer a next step.** Every error should suggest what to try
    25→- **"I/we" framing.** Collaborative, not diagnostic
    26→- **Forward momentum.** Success messages imply "ready for the next thing"
    27→- **Celebrate wins.** Even small ones. "Nice — that's looking solid."
    28→- **Normalize difficulty.** "This is a tricky one" not "this is simple"
    29→
    30→### Never Say
    31→- "Error:" as a prefix (use context-specific language)
    32→- "Invalid" (use "didn't match" or "unexpected")
    33→- "Failed" alone (always add what we're doing about it)
    34→- "You need to" (use "we can" or "try")
    35→- "Obviously" or "simply" (nothing is obvious when you're stuck)
    36→
    37→### Always Say
    38→- "Let me check..." (before investigating)
    39→- "That worked — " (on success, then what's next)
    40→- "Heads up:" (for non-blocking warnings)
    41→- "I'll try a different approach" (on failure recovery)
    42→- "Nice." / "Clean." / "Looking good." (genuine micro-affirmations)
    43→
    44→## Workflow Protocol
    45→
    46→### The Agent Loop
    47→1. **Orient** — Inspect the scene before touching anything
    48→2. **Plan** — Think through the approach (use extended thinking)
    49→3. **Execute** — One mutation per call, always
    50→4. **Verify** — Inspect the result of every mutation

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## What Is OTTO

# /research.agent System Prompt — Complete Content

This document establishes a **multimodal markdown system prompt standard** for research agents, designed with modularity, auditability, and extensibility as core principles.

## Key Structural Components

**[meta]**: Protocol version 2.0.0, specifying runtime compatibility (OpenAI GPT-4o, Anthropic Claude, agentic systems), schema formats (JSON, YAML, markdown, Python, shell), and namespaces (project, user, team, field).

**[instructions]**: Agent directives emphasizing phase-by-phase progression, slash-command invocation support (e.g., `/research Q="..." field="..." years=...`), dynamic context ingestion from files and commands, explicit tool declaration per phase, and mandatory audit logging.

**[ascii_diagrams]**: Visual representations of file structure, argument flow through phases, and slash-command mapping architecture.

**[context_schema]**: YAML specification defining research_query fields (question, field, scope, years, context, data_sources, constraints, args), session metadata (user, role, goal, priority_phases), and team composition.

**[workflow]**: Seven-phase pipeline—scope/context, search/gather, review/critique, synthesis, insight_mapping, gap_uncertainty, and audit_logging—each with defined outputs.

**[tools]**: Registry of four tools (web_search, summarize, evidence_mapper, audit_logger) with input/output schemas, protocol specifications, phase assignments, and usage examples.

**[recursion]**: Python function `research_agent_cycle()` implementing iterative refinement with depth limiting and revision logic.

**[examples]**: Practical demonstration of slash-command invocation, phase outputs formatted as tables, and complete audit trail documentation.

The design emphasizes transparent argument-passing, feedback loops, and comprehensive logging throughout the research workflow.

# /test.agent System Prompt - Complete Content

## Overview

This document defines a modular, extensible system prompt for test automation spanning generation, execution, mutation, coverage, and reporting. It's designed for agentic/CLI workflows with built-in audit capabilities.

## Core Structure

**[meta]** section declares protocol version 2.0.0, supporting multiple runtimes (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-4o, agentic systems) with audit logging enabled.

**[instructions]** establish that the agent accepts slash commands with arguments, file references, and shell output; processes tests phase-by-phase; and surfaces all failures and coverage gaps without suppression.

## Workflow Architecture

The system defines six sequential phases:

1. **context_suite_parsing** – Parse suite specs, flags, and files
2. **test_generation** – Generate/expand test cases for target suite
3. **mutation_testing** – Create test variants for fault injection
4. **test_execution** – Run tests and capture results
5. **coverage_analysis** – Measure coverage and identify gaps
6. **report_audit_logging** – Generate structured reports and audit trails

## Tools Registry

Seven internal tools manage each phase:
- suite_parser
- test_generator
- mutator
- test_executor
- coverage_analyzer
- audit_logger

Each tool specifies input/output schemas, protocol calls, and examples.

## Key Features

- **Recursion loop** supports up to 4 revision cycles based on test state
- **ASCII diagrams** visualize file structure and pipeline flow
- **Context schema** in YAML defines test_context, session, and team fields
- **Examples section** demonstrates slash command invocation, table outputs, and workflow visualization

The prompt emphasizes explicit tool declarations, audit readiness, and surfacing of failures throughout all phases.

# Complete Content: Atoms: The Fundamental Unit of Prompting

## Full Document

**Opening Quote:**
"If you wish to make an apple pie from scratch, you must first invent the universe." — Carl Sagan

**Main Sections:**

The document defines an **atom** as a single, standalone instruction to an LLM. It breaks down atomic prompt anatomy into three components: task, constraints, and output format.

The piece outlines five key limitations: "No memory across interactions, Limited demonstration capability, No complex reasoning scaffolds, Prone to ambiguity, High variance in outputs."

**Experimental Framework:**
The text presents Python code demonstrating variability in model responses when given identical prompts repeatedly, showing inconsistency problems.

**Core Concepts:**

- Atomic prompts serve as baseline measurements for token efficiency and response quality
- Models leverage implicit context from training data including grammar, common knowledge, and format conventions
- A power law relationship exists between context tokens and output quality, with a "maximum ROI zone"
- Diminishing returns occur when excessive tokens degrade performance

**Transition to Advanced Techniques:**
The document illustrates progression from simple atomic prompts to "molecules"—multi-part prompts combining instructions, examples, and structured formats.

**Practical Exercise:**
A table demonstrates three versions of summarization prompts with varying token counts (4-27) and quality ratings (2/10-8/10).

**Templates Provided:**
Six prompt template patterns: basic instruction, persona-based, format-specific, constraint-based, and step-by-step guided approaches.

**Final Takeaway:**
Atomic prompts form the foundation of LLM interaction, establishing control baselines before advancing to more sophisticated context engineering techniques.

## Summary: Existing Context Engineering / Prompt Infrastructure

The user has built a remarkably deep and sophisticated context engineering system across multiple layers. Here is what is already in place:

### 1. CLAUDE.md Hierarchy (Static Context Injection)

The user operates a **three-tier CLAUDE.md system** that Claude Code auto-loads:

| Tier | File | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| **Global** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Referenced in workspace file but **does not currently exist on disk** -- the workspace file at `C:\Users\User\CLAUDE.md` acts as the de facto global |
| **Workspace** | `C:\Users\User\CLAUDE.md` | Cross-project navigation map, shared patterns, platform constraints, domain laws |
| **Per-Project** | 19 project-specific `CLAUDE.md` files | Deep architecture docs, test commands, anti-patterns, gotchas |

The workspace-level `CLAUDE.md` (`C:\Users\User\CLAUDE.md`) is substantial (~115 lines) and contains:
- **Project map**: 11 active projects with test commands, 4 shipped/parked, 5 utilities
- **Cross-project conventions**: He2025 determinism patterns, testing rules, Windows gotchas
- **Domain laws**: PBR lighting law (intensity <= 1.0, exposure for brightness) -- marked "never violate"
- **Infrastructure map**: References to `~/.claude/`, `~/.synapse/`, `~/.orchestra/` directories
- **Hardware context**: Threadripper PRO 7965WX, RTX 4090, 128GB DDR5, Windows 11

Per-project CLAUDE.md files are extremely detailed (Orchestra's is 192 lines, Synapse's is 249 lines), covering architecture, anti-patterns, gotchas, testing patterns, and extension guides.

### 2. `~/.claude/` Directory (Claude Code Runtime State)

| Item | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `settings.local.json` | Permission allowlist for 23 pre-approved Bash/MCP commands |
| `projects/C--Users-User/` | 10+ session JSONL logs with tool results and subagent transcripts |
| `projects/C--Users-User-JaimeIbrahim/` | Separate project session history (3 subagents) |
| `projects/C--Users-User-SYNAPSE/` | Synapse project session history |
| `todos/` | 10 task JSON files from agent sessions |
| `debug/` | Debug logs per session |
| `history.jsonl` | Command history across sessions |
| `cache/changelog.md` | Claude Code changelog cache |

**Notable absence**: The `substrate/` directory referenced in the CLAUDE.md (`substrate/tools/` with 293 tests, `substrate/knowledge/` with 89 prims) **does not exist at `~/.claude/substrate/`**. It appears to live inside the Orchestra project at `src/orchestra/substrate/` instead. The workspace CLAUDE.md is slightly aspirational or outdated on this point.

Similarly, `~/.claude/projects/_index.md` and `~/.claude/session_state.json` (referenced in the CLAUDE.md) **do not exist on disk**.

### 3. Orchestra -- Cognitive Safety Layer (`~/.orchestra/`)

Orchestra v7.1.0 is a **runtime cognitive state tracker** that sits between the user and Claude Code:

- **`~/.orchestra/state/cognitive_state.json`**: Tracks 19+ fields including altitude, burnout level (green), energy level (medium), momentum phase (cold_start), tangent budget, epistemic tension, convergence attractor
- **`~/.orchestra/bcm/trail_default.json`**: BCM (stigmergic learning) trail with 2-hour decay half-life -- currently empty/initialized state
- **Hook integration**: Claude Code calls `python -m orchestra.hooks` via stdin/stdout to get `[EXEC:checksum|expert|paradigm|altitude|depth|source_mode]` anchors
- **8-Phase NEXUS Pipeline**: RETRIEVE -> CLASSIFY -> GROUND -> DETECT -> CASCADE -> LOCK -> EXECUTE -> UPDATE
- **Safety gating**: Automatically reduces thinking depth when user is depleted/burned out

### 4. Synapse -- AI-Houdini Bridge Memory System (`~/.synapse/`)

Synapse v5.2.0 has its own **persistent project memory** system:

- **Per-project memory**: `$HIP/.synapse/memory.jsonl` (append-only), `index.json` (search indices), `context.md`, `decisions.md`, `tasks.md`
